clinician.trajectory_summary: A 59-year-old man presented with neurological symptoms including expressive aphasia, memory deficits, confusion, staring spells, and right hand spasms. Brain MRI before admission showed a large confluent area of abnormal signal in the left medial temporal lobe and hippocampus. Chest CT identified a partially calcified 4.0×2.3×1.5 cm anterior mediastinal mass most likely thymoma. Serum testing found positive muscle acetylcholine receptor binding antibody. The patient underwent video assisted thoracoscopic surgery with histopathology confirming type B2–B3 thymoma. Post-surgical and immunotherapy treatment led to significant resolution of brain lesions on follow-up MRI and clinical improvement.
